questions.text: Write about the importance of the Kalinga War.
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the importance of the Kalinga War. (Difficult)

answer.value:
Kalinga War:
Ashoka waged war on the Kalinga kingdom in the eighth year of his reign. The Kalinga kingdom, now part of modern-day Odisha, was the site of Ashoka's war. Thousands of people lost their lives in the war, a hundred thousand were wounded, and one hundred and fifty thousand enemy soldiers were captured. The horrific scenes of death and suffering on the battlefield deeply moved Ashoka. From that moment, Ashoka decided not to wage war again. Emperor Ashoka, whose mind was thus transformed and who chose the path of Dharma instead of war, is revered as "Mahaashaya" (the Great One).

questions.text: Explain the contribution of the Guptas to Sanskrit literature.

During the Gupta period, Sanskrit literature flourished under royal patronage.
Kalidasa composed four epic poems and three plays. Abhijnanashakuntalam is considered his greatest play, and he is praised as "Kavikula Guru" (Teacher of Poets).

questions.text: Discuss Nalanda University.
questions.text_as_printed: Discuss Nalanda University. (Difficult)

answer.value:
Nalanda University:
Nalanda University, in present Bihar state, was famous for more than six centuries from the times of the Gupta period.
It was a famous university in ancient India.
Thousands of students from foreign countries like Japan and China used to come here to study.
There were eight large schools and three large libraries.
Although Buddhism was the main subject of study here, Veda, Yoga, medicine and other subjects were also taught.
In due course of time, on account of many attacks, the books in the University were set on fire and great scholars died, and Nalanda University lost its reputation.
